kinds.unverified: Could not be confirmed from an official source
kinds.irregular: Official sources disagree or contain an error

flags.title: Your own facts were not provided
flags.detail: Source of the yuan, whether Chinese tax was paid on it, the identity document your bank holds for you, when the yuan was acquired, your US institution and your filing history are all unknown. Eligibility and tax cells that depend on them are blank.
flags.affects: Which method you may use; Chinese tax; US currency gain; US penalties.

flags.title: The exchange rate is one board snapshot
flags.detail: All conversions use the Bank of China board row published 2026/11/10 17:39:58. The board is marked for reference only; the executed rate is the one in the bank's channel at the time.
flags.affects: Every USD figure derived from yuan.

flags.title: Intermediary-bank deductions on a standard wire
flags.detail: Without the full-amount option, Bank of China passes on foreign banks' charges at cost. No amount is published, so the standard-wire total is not shown; the tables price the full-amount option instead.

flags.title: HSBC China's exchange rate
flags.detail: HSBC China's customer rate for USD was not read. Its conversion margin and therefore its all-in cost are blank; only its published fees are shown.

flags.title: HSBC China full-amount delivery has no fixed price
flags.detail: The tariff collects CNY 200 up front for full-amount USD delivery and bills any shortfall after the overseas bank's notice.

flags.title: ICBC's remittance fees are published only as an image
flags.detail: The international-business section of ICBC's price list is an image file, so no figure could be read. No ICBC row is given.

flags.title: China Merchants Bank and China Construction Bank fees
flags.detail: Figures found on official pages are undated (CMB) or from 2016 (CCB). They are listed under sources as seen but are not used in any cost table.

flags.title: Wise fees are time-stamped quotes and depend on monthly volume
flags.detail: Four quotes were read on 2026-11-10. Wise says large-transfer discounts carry over to eligible transfers for the rest of the month, so rows built from separate single-transfer quotes may overstate the fee.

flags.title: Receiving fee for a Wise payout
flags.detail: Wise pays out by local US bank transfer. The Chase fee schedule read lists wire fees only; whether a receiving institution charges for this kind of credit was not confirmed. The Wise table shows Wise's fee alone.

flags.title: Cross-border RMB: where to receive it and at what rate
flags.detail: Which institutions outside mainland China will receive yuan for a US citizen, and their conversion rates, were not researched. Only the Chinese bank's sending fee is shown.

flags.title: ATM route: network rate, owner surcharge and machine limits
flags.detail: The UnionPay conversion rate, the ATM owner's surcharge and each machine's withdrawal limit were not verified. The table assumes withdrawals of CNY 10,000 each (the per-card daily cap) and shows Bank of China's fee only.

flags.title: Bank of China's overseas ATM price changes on 11 Nov 2026
flags.detail: From 2026-11-11 UnionPay withdrawals abroad stay at CNY 12 plus 1% (maximum CNY 112); Mastercard and Visa withdrawals become 2.5%, minimum USD 3, maximum USD 40.

flags.title: Card purchases abroad: issuer fee and network rate
flags.detail: No official figure was read for the cost of card purchases abroad. The table for M12 is blank.

flags.title: Cash routes: travel cost and the rate for yuan notes abroad
flags.detail: Travel cost has no official price. The rate for exchanging yuan banknotes outside China was not verified. The cash tables show trips needed and, for USD cash, the bank's conversion margin only.

flags.title: Which tax paper a foreign individual needs above USD 50,000
flags.detail: The 2013 tax-filing notice lists a foreign individual's China pay among payments needing a filing above USD 50,000, and also says foreign individuals follow the personal foreign-exchange rules. SAFE Xiamen accepts either the filing form or a tax payment certificate. The sources do not settle which one a given bank will ask for.

flags.title: Property-sale proceeds: SAFE approval or bank only
flags.detail: The 2006 central-bank measures say a foreign individual's home-sale yuan may be converted with SAFE approval. SAFE Xiamen (2021) says such sales are handled directly at the bank, and the 2025 SAFE guide lists bank documents only. Treat the bank-only procedure as current and confirm with the bank.

flags.title: Two official definitions of who counts as a domestic individual
flags.detail: The State Council regulation counts a foreigner who has lived in China continuously for one year as a domestic individual. The central-bank measures and SAFE guidance classify by identity document: a passport holder is an overseas individual with no purchase quota. Banks apply the document test.
flags.affects: Whether the USD 50,000 quota is available.

flags.title: Errors inside the SAFE Hebei service guides
flags.detail: The emigrant guide cites 国税发〔2005〕13号 where the inheritance guide cites 国税发〔2005〕16号 for the same notice. The inheritance guide also repeats the emigrant condition that the assets were held before acquiring foreign status, which the inheritance definition does not contain.

flags.title: The 2004 transfer measures still display repealed terms
flags.detail: The published text keeps the two-year staged schedule and the referral of amounts above CNY 500,000 to SAFE headquarters. Both were removed by the 2014 notice.

flags.title: No Chinese conversion tax is an absence finding
flags.detail: The statement that China does not tax the conversion rests on no such tax appearing in the rules read, not on an official sentence saying so.

flags.title: Chinese taxes on the money itself were not computed
flags.detail: Only the statutory rate bands were read. Taxes on a home sale, the treatment of deposit interest, and any tax-treaty relief were not researched.

flags.title: Currency-gain figures are an illustration
flags.detail: They use IRS yearly average rates in place of the actual rates on the days the yuan was acquired; the IRS table stops at 2025, so yuan acquired in 2026 is not covered. Whether your holding is a personal transaction, and your tax rate, are not decided here, so no tax amount is shown.

flags.title: Form 3520 penalty rate
flags.detail: The IRS page read refers to penalties under section 6039F(c) without giving the rate. The cell is blank.

flags.title: The IRS page for delinquent FBAR procedures returns Error 404
flags.detail: The long-standing address no longer resolves. The rule is quoted from the Taxpayer Advocate Service page instead.

flags.title: FBAR penalty figures are the 2025 adjustment
flags.detail: The regulation's table, current as of 6 Nov 2026, gives amounts for penalties assessed on or after 17 Jan 2025 and shows no later adjustment.

flags.title: US Customs states the cash threshold two ways
flags.detail: One release says more than USD 10,000 must be reported; another says USD 10,000 or greater in one sentence and more than USD 10,000 in the next.

flags.title: Scope of the US 1% remittance tax
flags.detail: The IRS text read describes a tax paid by a sender who funds a remittance transfer with cash or a similar instrument. The statute's definitions were not opened to confirm that a wire arriving from China is outside it.

flags.title: Some sources were confirmed from an excerpt only
flags.detail: Sources marked Excerpt on the sources page were read as text returned by the search tool from the official address; the page itself was not opened. Open the link to confirm.

flags.title: Bank processing times
flags.detail: No official processing time was found for bank conversion and wire steps. Time cells for those methods are blank.

flags.title: The board's reference column sits above the selling price
flags.detail: On the snapshot the 中行折算价 is 671.67 while the selling price is 668.51. It is not used as a midpoint.

flags.title: SAFE Xiamen guidance dates from 2021
flags.detail: It is the clearest official statement that foreign passport holders have no purchase quota and that home sales are handled at the bank, but it predates the 2025 notice.

flags.title: Typing errors in the IRS exchange-rate table
flags.detail: The Euro Zone 2024 cell reads 0,924 and the Russia 2021 cell reads .73.686. The China row is unaffected.

flags.title: HSBC Global Transfers between your own HSBC accounts
flags.detail: Official HSBC China documents describe free same-name transfers for Premier customers, but they are undated and the current tariff line was not read. Not priced.

flags.title: Routes not researched in this edition
flags.detail: Company profit or dividend remittance, insurance payouts, Western Union and similar agents, Hong Kong accounts and investment schemes were not researched here. Earlier editions in this repository cover some of them.
